subject: Religionskunskap
title: Islam
sourceSummary: The fundamental beliefs of Islam, the five pillars, the difference between Sunni and Shia, and the Quran and important festivals such as Ramadan — the basis for understanding the world's second-largest religion.

questions.prompt: What is at the heart of Islam's belief in God?
questions.opener: The word "Islam" roughly means "submission" — submission to what?
choices: That there are several gods who rule different parts of the world
That there is only one God, Allah, who is the same as the God of Judaism and Christianity
questions.explanation: Islam is a strictly monotheistic religion — believers hold that there is one single God, Allah, who within Islam is seen as the same God as in Judaism and Christianity, but with a different revelation. Muhammad is regarded as a prophet, not as God.

questions.prompt: What role does Muhammad have within Islam?
questions.opener: Think about what Muslims believe Muhammad received, and from whom.
choices: He is regarded as God on Earth
He is seen as the last and most important prophet, who received the revelations of the Quran from Allah
He wrote the Quran as an ordinary literary work with no divine origin
questions.explanation: Within Islam, Muhammad is seen as the last and most important prophet, through whom the Quran was revealed by Allah via the angel Gabriel. He is not regarded as divine, but as a human being and messenger.

questions.prompt: Which of the five pillars involves fasting for an entire month?
questions.opener: The fast is linked to a specific month in the Islamic calendar.
questions.explanation: During Ramadan, Muslims fast from dawn until sunset as one of the five pillars. Shahada is the declaration of faith, zakat is almsgiving, and hajj is the pilgrimage to Mecca.

questions.opener: Think of one of the pillars that is about sharing financially.
choices: Giving a set proportion of one's wealth to the poor and needy
questions.explanation: Zakat is almsgiving — a religious duty to give a fixed portion of one's wealth to the poor and needy. Prayer is called salat, the pilgrimage hajj, and the fast Ramadan.

questions.prompt: What was the original point of dispute that led to the split between Sunni and Shia Muslims?
questions.opener: Think about what happened right after Muhammad died — who was to take over the leadership.
choices: Which prayer should be said first in the day
Who should succeed Muhammad as leader of the Muslims
Whether the Quran should exist in Arabic or not
Whether Ramadan should be celebrated or not
questions.explanation: The split arose over the question of who should become Muhammad's successor (caliph). Shia Muslims believed leadership should stay within Muhammad's family, while Sunni Muslims accepted an elected successor. The issue was therefore about leadership, not about prayers or language.

questions.prompt: What is the Quran, according to Muslim belief?
questions.opener: Compare this with how the Bible is described within Christianity, but notice the difference in how it came about.
choices: A historical novel written by several authors over a long period
God's own words, revealed to Muhammad through the angel Gabriel
A collection of myths with no religious significance for Muslims today
A book that is only about Muhammad's life
questions.explanation: Within Islam, the Quran is seen as God's direct, unchanged words, revealed to Muhammad through the angel Gabriel over some twenty years. This differs from the Bible, which within Christianity is often seen as written by people inspired by God.

questions.prompt: Describe all five pillars of Islam and briefly explain why they are together important for a Muslim's life of faith.
questions.opener: Go through the pillars one by one: faith, prayer, almsgiving, fasting, pilgrimage.
questions.answer: The five pillars are: 1) Shahada, the declaration of faith ("there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is his prophet"). 2) Salat, the daily prayer performed five times a day. 3) Zakat, almsgiving to the poor. 4) Sawm, fasting during Ramadan. 5) Hajj, the pilgrimage to Mecca at least once in a lifetime for those who have the health and means to do so. Together, the pillars form a practical foundation for how a Muslim lives out their faith every day, every week, every year, and at least once in a lifetime.
steps: Shahada is the declaration of faith itself — the foundation all the other pillars build on.
Salat takes place daily, five times, keeping prayer present in everyday life.
Zakat links faith to social responsibility by sharing with those in need.
Sawm during Ramadan is about self-discipline and reminding oneself of those who are struggling.
Hajj is a pilgrimage carried out at least once in a lifetime, if one is able, and binds Muslims worldwide together around a shared place: Mecca.

questions.prompt: Summarise the foundations of Islam: belief in God, Muhammad, the five pillars, Sunni/Shia, and the Quran.
questions.opener: Split the answer into faith, prophet, pillars, branches, and holy scripture.
questions.answer: Belief in God: Islam is monotheistic — one single God, Allah. Muhammad: seen as the last prophet, received the revelations of the Quran via the angel Gabriel. The five pillars: shahada (declaration of faith) · salat (prayer five times a day) · zakat (almsgiving) · sawm (fasting during Ramadan) · hajj (pilgrimage to Mecca). Sunni and Shia: the two largest branches, originally split over the question of who should succeed Muhammad as leader — Sunni is by far the largest branch globally. The Quran: Islam's holy scripture, seen as God's own words in Arabic. Ramadan: the month of fasting, one of the year's most important festivals, ending with the festival of Eid al-Fitr.

questions.prompt: Which city is considered Islam's holiest site, where Muslims make pilgrimage during Hajj?
questions.opener: The city is located in modern-day Saudi Arabia.
questions.explanation: Mecca is considered Islam's holiest city, with the Kaaba as the pilgrims' destination during Hajj. Medina is Islam's second-holiest city.

questions.prompt: Which pillar is the declaration of faith, stating that there is only one God and that Muhammad is his prophet?
questions.opener: This pillar is often considered the foundation all the other pillars rest on.
questions.explanation: Shahada is the declaration of faith - stating that there is only one God (Allah) and that Muhammad is his prophet. It's the first and most fundamental of the five pillars.

questions.prompt: How many times a day do practising Muslims pray according to the pillar of salat?
questions.opener: The prayer times are spread across the day, from dawn to evening.
questions.explanation: Salat means praying five times a day at set times: dawn, midday, afternoon, sunset and evening.

questions.prompt: Roughly what share of the world's Muslims belong to the Sunni branch?
questions.opener: It's by far the larger of the two main branches.
questions.explanation: Roughly 85-90 percent of the world's Muslims are considered Sunni, while Shia Muslims make up roughly 10-15 percent, with Iran being one of the countries where Shia Islam is the majority.

questions.prompt: Which festival marks the end of the fasting month of Ramadan?
questions.opener: The name roughly means "festival of breaking the fast".
questions.explanation: Eid al-Fitr is celebrated when Ramadan ends and marks the close of the fasting month, often with shared meals, prayer and gifts.

questions.prompt: Explain why Hajj, the pilgrimage to Mecca, is considered one of Islam's most important acts, and what is required for a Muslim to need to perform it.
questions.opener: Think about what happens when millions of people from around the world gather in the same place, dressed the same way.
questions.answer: Hajj brings together Muslims from around the world at a single holy site, strengthening the sense of community (ummah) and equality before God, since all pilgrims wear simple, identical clothing regardless of social status. According to Islamic tradition, Hajj is obligatory at least once in a lifetime, but only for those who have sufficient health and financial resources to make the journey.
steps: Hajj takes place once a year in the city of Mecca and brings together millions of Muslims from around the world.
During the pilgrimage, all pilgrims wear simple, white garments (ihram), which erases visible differences in wealth or status.
This strengthens the experience of equality and community (ummah) among Muslims regardless of background.

According to Islamic tradition, Hajj is one of the five pillars and obligatory at least once in a lifetime - but only for those with the health and financial resources to manage the journey, making the duty conditional rather than absolute for everyone.

questions.prompt: What is the holy city called that Muhammad, according to tradition, fled to in 622, an event marking the start of the Islamic calendar?
questions.opener: The city is Islam's second-holiest, after Mecca.
questions.explanation: Muhammad's flight (hijra) to Medina in 622 marks the start of the Islamic calendar. Medina is considered Islam's second-holiest city, after Mecca.
